paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: Historical domestic production and regional crushing heartland for peninsular black-soil sunflower.

paragraphs.text: 2. Kakinada–Chennai Port-Based Refining Mega-Hub (Andhra Pradesh & Tamil Nadu)
Strategic Role: Center of the Indian sunflower oil market; handles massive volumes of ocean-borne crude oil imports for refining and packaging.

Key Facilities: Continuous physical/chemical edible oil refineries (Adani Wilmar, Gemini Edibles, Ruchi Soya/Patanjali, Kaleesuwari) located along the Kakinada, Krishnapatnam, and Chennai port belts; deepwater liquid cargo docks connected via heated pipelines directly into shore-tank farms.

Catchment Areas: Refines imported crude oil to meet consumer demand across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala, while processing secondary regional domestic seed arrivals from the Krishna-Godavari and coastal Odisha basins.

summary.text: Despite strong consumer demand for refined sunflower oil in urban households (which drives massive raw oil imports), India’s domestic seed production has faced severe acreage contraction over the past two decades. Domestic acreage fell from over 2.0–2.5 million hectares in the late 1990s to under 0.25 million hectares currently, driven by severe disease outbreaks, high seed costs, competition from maize and Bt cotton, and bird depredation.

protection.name: Sunflower Necrosis Disease (SND) (Tobacco Streak Virus transmitted by Thrips Scirtothrips dorsalis, Frankliniella schultzei)
protection.geography: National Epidemic Hazard (Heavy in Kharif peninsular crops)
protection.impact: Systemic viral necrosis; young leaves develop chlorotic rings and mosaic mottling; midribs and petioles show dark brown necrotic streaks; stem twists and head deforms into an "S"-shaped crook ("stem necrosis"); complete floral head malformation and sterile, seedless chaff; causes 30–80% crop destruction.
protection.passage: Sunflower — source table 170, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Alternaria Leaf Blight (Alternaria helianthi, A. alternata)
protection.geography: All-India Commercial Belts (Heavy in warm, humid spells)
protection.impact: Small, dark brown-to-black circular spots with concentric rings appear on lower leaves; lesions coalesce into large irregular necrotic blights; spreads upward to petioles, stems, and ray florets; causes premature leaf drying, severe defoliation ("leaf firing"), and stunted heads with shriveled seeds; reduces seed yield by 20–50%.
protection.passage: Sunflower — source table 170, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Downy Mildew (Plasmopara halstedii)
protection.impact: Systemic dwarfing; plants remain severely stunted (20–40 cm tall) with thickened, rigid, chlorotic pale-yellow leaves; a thick, white, downy fungal mat coats the lower leaf surfaces; heads point straight up toward the sky ("erect heads") and remain completely sterile; causes 20–60% field mortality.
protection.passage: Sunflower — source table 170, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Head Borer / Capitulum Borer (Helicoverpa armigera)
protection.geography: Flowering to Head-Filling Stages (All Commercial Belts)
protection.impact: Moths lay small, ribbed, yellowish eggs on involucral bracts and opening florets; larvae chew into the floral head, feeding on disc florets and boring through developing achenes; causes extensive seed hollowing; entrance tunnels accumulate moist brown larval frass, predisposing heads to secondary bacterial rot.
protection.passage: Sunflower — source table 170, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Rhizopus Head Rot & Sclerotium Wilt (Rhizopus arrhizus, Sclerotium rolfsii)
protection.impact:
Head Rot: Water-soaked soft rotting of the capitulum receptacle; head tissues turn brown and disintegrate into a wet, stringy mass covered in coarse black-spored fungal mycelium.

Sclerotium Wilt: White fan-like mycelium with tiny brown mustard-seed-like sclerotia girdles the stem collar, causing sudden plant collapse.
protection.passage: Sunflower — source table 170, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Rust-Red Flour Beetle & Rice Weevil (Tribolium castaneum, Sitophilus oryzae)
protection.impact: Beetles and larvae penetrate cracked or broken achene hulls; feed internally on oil- and protein-rich cotyledons, increasing free fatty acid (FFA) levels and turning oil rancid; reduces germination vigour.
protection.passage: Sunflower — source table 170, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
